title: Ahead of Ozzy Osbourne ‘Prince of Darkness’ Haunted House’s Debut at Universal Orlando, Check Out These Crazy Scary Photos
summary: The late heavy metal icon’s son Jack and widow Sharon were heavily involved in everything from story creation to approving scene design.
contentText:
From the looks of it, the Ozzy Osbourne : Prince of Darkness haunted house at Universal Orlando Resort will be a trick and a treat for fans of the late heavy metal icon.

In a preview of the attraction that is debuting at the theme park this week, Charles Gray, senior show director, entertainment creative development for the Florida park, tells Billboard that Ozzy’s son Jack Osbourne and widow/manager Sharon Osbourne were intimately involved in the planning and execution of the attraction that will make its debut during the park’s annual Halloween Horror Nights.

“Jack and Sharon were with us every step of the way,” says Gray. “They embraced our story and creative and inspected and approved all elements from scenic design to mask sculpts.”

Gray adds that the goal was to create an original story within an “Ozzy-inspired world” that would provide a fan-first experience that even the Halloween-loving Blizzard of Ozz himself would enjoy walking through. “It was important for us to create something we think he would enjoy and to pay homage to his music and legacy,” he says.

The creative team at the park did that by using Ozzy’s album covers as the jumping-off point, then following the evolution of the rock icon’s music and persona, with songs from his different solo eras propelling guests through the story. Among the iconic needle drops are his 1983 solo hit “Bark at the Moon,” as well as a mash-up of “Crazy Train” (which finally cracked the Billboard Hot 100 at No. 39 following the singer’s death in 2025) and “Mr. Tinkertrain” in a train-station set paying homage to a young Ozzy’s life growing up in Birmingham, England, and riding the train to and from London.

Asked to rate the attraction from mild jump scare to 10+ terrifying, Gray teases that “there is so much to take in both with the audio and visually that the scares appear right on top of you. The distraction scares are on point!”

The experience marking Halloween Horror Nights’ 35th anniversary will cover 45 years of Osbourne’s career, opening Friday (Aug. 28) and running through Nov. 1 at the Orlando resort; Universal Studios Hollywood will present a different iteration of the haunted house on the West Coast from Sept. 3-Nov. 1.

Osbourne  died July 22, 2025 , at age 76, just weeks after Black Sabbath’s final concert on July 5 in his hometown of Birmingham. The attraction will feature music from throughout Osbourne’s solo career, including the solo albums:  The Blizzard of Ozz  (1980),  Diary of a Madman  (1981),  Bark at the Moon  (1983),  No More Tears  (1991),  Scream  (2010) and  Ordinary Man  (2020). 

In July, Sharon Osbourne told Entertainment Weekly that the famously mischievous, horror-loving Ozzy would have “absolutely” loved the attraction. “I’m sure he’s looking down smiling,” she said, adding that he’d be “laughing his head off” given how much he loved horror movies and Halloween. “He used to joke that every day was Halloween in our house, so this couldn’t be more fitting.”

Check out five exclusive preview images from Universal Orlando Resort’s Prince of Darkness attraction, with captions courtesy of Gray.

Opening statement and façade of the “Ozzy Osbourne: Prince of Darkness” haunted house. It has high level textures and lighting that focus in on the dark fantasy elements that are reminiscent of the Ozzy album covers.

Courtesy of Universal Orlando Resort

Entrance into the Crazy Train. Guests will travel through the belly of the beast and the train’s furnace.

Last stop of the Crazy Train. It is a world covered in industrial pollution and Black Rain (one of my favorite albums). Guests will feel the rain as they are hunted by victims of this apocalyptic landscape.

Final scene of the haunted house and the throne room of the Prince of Darkness. Similar to his farewell concert, Ozzy will be sitting on the throne next to his Ozzy Dragon from the Ultimate Sin album. Lava and fire surround the rock structures that create the dais for the Prince of Darkness.

Inside the Crazy Train, guests are surrounded by a hellish and kinetic world both outside and inside the train cars. They will see and feel themselves going off the rails on the Crazy Train while being pursued by impish stowaways. It’s “crazy, but that’s how it goes.”
